Full field layout of segmented callback list, plain callback list and grace period sequence structures.
Semantics of sequence comparison helpers and grace period state encodings.
Complete scale test thread lifecycles, duration sampling and statistics reporting.
Behavior of normal versus expedited funnel start and barrier sequences beyond invocation points.
Handlers for per CPU callback work, delay timer, interrupt work and boot list draining.

findings.text: Segmented callback accelerator merges later pending groups into an earlier eligible group and labels the merged group with the caller supplied grace period position, reporting whether any movement happened.
Acceleration expects an enabled list, leaves done callbacks untouched, does nothing when no pending callbacks exist beyond done, and preserves segments older than the selected merge point.

Callback storage progresses through ordered stages from newest arrival through ready and waiting to done, with acceleration moving callbacks forward in grace period terms and advancement moving matured callbacks to done followed by compaction.

List merging relocates both completed and not yet completed callbacks from a source list into a destination list, accounting for counts and linkage in the destination, then returns the source to an empty initialized condition.
Merging assumes callers exclude CPU hotplug removal so that length clearing and barrier interactions remain safe without additional ordering.

Sleepable RCU advancement compares each intermediate segment normal sequence against a supplied sequence, promotes all preceding segments to done with length transfer, and compacts only when at least one segment moved.

Sleepable RCU acceleration reuses the generic accelerator by constructing a grace period descriptor whose normal component carries the caller sequence and whose expedited component is marked untracked.

Scale harness write blocks link an RCU callback header with a lock free list node and a back pointer to an owning freelist, while freelists pair global and per thread queues with an inflight count and a block array.

Scale operations form a flavor abstraction carrying a type tag, lifecycle hooks, read section entry and exit, sequence query and difference, expedited completion query, asynchronous and barrier and synchronous waits, an optional grace thread accessor and statistics hook, plus a name.
Maximum measurement count is 10000 and minimum measurement count is 100.
Scale log marker is the string -scale: and the default test flavor name is rcu.

Standard RCU flavor for scaling enters and exits a read section, reports zero for an unused completion query, performs no special init, and binds hurry asynchronous, barrier, normal synchronous and expedited synchronous operations under the name rcu.

Sleepable RCU flavor for scaling uses a global control pointer, acquires and releases sleepable read sections returning an index cookie, queries completed batch count, and forwards asynchronous callbacks to sleepable queueing.
Completed batch query returns the current grace period sequence value held in the shared sleepable control block.

Tiny sleepable queueing attaches the callback to the tail of a single global queue and then ensures a grace period is pending, with the linkage update performed with preemption disabled and interrupts saved.

Tiny grace period initiation derives a cookie from the current index, ignores the request when the recorded maximum already covers that cookie, otherwise records the new maximum and either queues interrupt work after early init or links onto a boot list before init completes.
Tree sleepable queueing validates the callback header for prior queueing, and on suspected duplicate replaces the function with a leak handler, warns once, and drops the new request without enqueue.

Tree grace period initiation runs inside a non migratable sleepable read section, chooses boot CPU or local per CPU state based on sizing progress and online status, and serializes enqueue plus sequence updates under the per CPU lock with interrupts disabled.

Tree initiation captures the acceleration snapshot before reading the current sequence for advancement, so a grace period completing between those steps cannot cause the fresh callback to miss its target and remain stuck in the newest segment.

Per CPU locking first attempts an immediate acquisition and on contention briefly takes the shared control lock to account retries before acquiring the per CPU lock, allowing contention accounting to trigger growth.

Sleepable control sizing starts small, moves to allocation requested either directly when non preemptible or after node allocation succeeds, then waits for barrier before becoming big, with a contention path forcing allocation after repeated retries within the same tick when enabled.
Lazy initialization uses an acquire check of the needed sequence state for the fast path and otherwise serializes one time field setup under the shared control lock with recheck inside.

Control initialization prepares locks and mutexes, sequence numbers, barrier state, delayed and interrupt work, per CPU storage and node geometry as appropriate for static or dynamic objects, and publishes completion with release ordering.

Per CPU sleepable state starts with an empty callback list, non invoking flag, needed sequences equal to the current sequence, a self linked barrier list, no parent node, assigned CPU number, callback work, delay timer and back pointer to the control.

Node tree setup allocates one array for all levels, assigns level bases, initializes locks and callback presence markers and group extents, links non root nodes to parents by spread geometry, then attaches each CPU to a leaf while expanding group ranges and computing a group mask.
Offload status reports true only when the corresponding build option is enabled and the offloaded flag is set, otherwise false.
Callback count query observes the list length with single access ordering without modifying state.
Duplicate sleepable enqueue does not corrupt the queue but intentionally leaks the callback after warning, so callers must not queue the same header twice without completion.
Failure of acceleration after a successful advance signals an ordering or sequence invariant breach and is reported as a one time warning rather than silent stall.
Scale messaging prefixes output with the active flavor name and marker, with verbose messages emitted only when verbosity is enabled and error messages adding an alert marker.

Scale harness tracks desired versus realized reader writer and expedited counts, task pointers, per writer duration tables and completion flags, freelists, start and finish timestamps and batch boundaries.
